\documentclass[11pt]{article}\usepackage[margin=1in]{geometry}\usepackage{amsmath,amsthm}\newtheorem{theorem}{Theorem}\newtheorem{remark}{Remark}
\title{Adaptive Retained-State Filtration for Dispersion Witnesses}\author{}\date{21 July 2026}\begin{document}\maketitle
\begin{abstract}We specify the adaptive interface required to turn low/high-dispersion estimates into a volume-uniform bad-block process while retaining the labels that carry frustration and topology.\end{abstract}
The retained state contains dispersion class, Fr\'echet-center chart, center flux, boundary holonomy, orbit chart, and topology sector. Only positive-probability histories generated by the declared exposure are quantified.
\begin{theorem}[Shared-uniform coupling]If every generated history $h$ satisfies
\[\Pr(X_{n+1}=1\mid h)\le q,
\]
then on a common sequence of independent uniforms the entire bad field is coordinatewise dominated by independent Bernoulli$(q)$. If $e^\alpha D^2q<1$, its rooted weighted connected sum is at most $e^\alpha q/(1-e^\alpha D^2q)$.\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}At each step compare the conditional threshold with the same uniform used for the Bernoulli variable. Induction preserves coordinatewise domination. The connected-set estimate is a geometric sum.\end{proof}
The executable schema also proves the union bound $q=q_{\rm low}+q_{\rm high}$ and rejects incomplete history tables. The two-site law supported on $01$ and $10$ falsifies promotion from intersection moments alone; an erased two-state example falsifies removal of rare-entry information.
\begin{remark}The theorem is exact, but the complete nonlinear Yang--Mills history table has not been established.\end{remark}\end{document}
